en: As for Rubbe and Tucke's Mika-chan, why, they're right across the street from your place. It's at the south end of Tsumugi Street.
Oh, for real? Yeesh. I hate the idea of Uno-san shuffling around with a stiffy in his slacks so close to home.
Well, I guess we should get going. Thanks, man. You're a lifesaver.
Just doing my job, friend. Good luck on your search!
The long-awaited Operation Panties... begins now.
So maybe this gal's a little older and has some experience under her garter, but her body looks ready to rock. If your guy had any money, he'd be in cream city by now.
Ah, so you would think!
Welcome! Just the two of you today?
No, we're just wondering if a middle-aged guy came by looking for your new girl. A little threadbare up top?
Hmm? Nope, haven't seen anyone like that.

There you have it. Uno-san's passion for amateurs runs deep.
Even deeper than beauty itself.
His passion is deeply misguided.
Well, that just leaves Rubbe and Tucke's. Shall we?

(I should be able to find a fashion magazine here. Might
give me some useful tips...)

(Leon, the fashion magazine for grown-up lady-killers. This
could be the ticket.)
(Hmm, all right. "Ladies love a mature man with a dash of roguish appeal.")

(The point is to dress appropriately and fashionably but
accentuate it with a slight debonair touch.)

(This makes men seem more open and approachable, thereby
upping their charm with the ladies.)

(Oh, hey, this is what I'm wearing. Hana-chan got it for me
for my birthday.)

(With such a bold design, this thing stands out like a neon
sign.)

(I see. Something like that might be all a guy needs to give
himself that roguish, playful look without overdoing it.)

(Okay, this could be just what Miyu-chan is looking for.
Saida-san needs to hear this.)

(So, this is the cursed PrintCircle. Those girls said a
ghost sometimes appears in the background. Should I take a
picture?)

(Nah, forget it. It's kind of lame for a grown man to do
this by himself.)

(Yeesh, I'm flat broke. Not even enough loose change for
PrintCircle...)

(Well, I came out here to investigate. I may as well see
this through.)
(Okay, let's see how they turned out.)
(This is the ghost!? That's as fake as they come!)
That's the ghost! Hey! Hold it!

(He hasn't come out yet. Should I go in and see how he's
doing?)
(I'll just wait and see.)

(Okay, Kushikatsu Daruma's chairman asked me to find out
about some tasty regional specialties. I wonder if now's a
good time to ask.)
(No, it can wait.)
(Sure, why not ask them now?)
Pardon me, gents. A moment of your time?
You need somethin'?

...And so I was hoping to hit you three up for ideas on
regional specialties that might be good as deep-fried
skewers.
Regional specialties, huh? I didn't pay much attention to food when I was down south.
I was on the lam. Wasn't doin' much dining out.

I'm always hurting for cash. I can't afford to eat all that
well.

Guess I picked the wrong panel of experts... Well, nothing
I can do about it now. I promised the man, so allow me to
at least get your opinions.
Mind if I start with you, Kiryu-san?

Kiryu-san, you were in Nagasugai, Fukuoka, right? Were
there any local specialties you'd recommend?

The president of the company I worked for treated me to a
great mizutaki stew.

Mizutaki stew, huh? It's a delicious hot pot with many
regional variations, sure, but how exactly does one make
that into fried skewers?
Well... Honestly, I couldn't tell you.

Hmm. Well, I'll be sure to pass that onto the chairman.
Thank you.

Mentaiko, I'd say. There was a shop famous for the spicy
fish roe in Nagasugai, too.

Oh, I see. That's rather intriguing, actually. I'm curious
as to what it would taste like as kushikatsu.
Thank you. That was quite a noteworthy suggestion.

How about soba noodles? I was broke, so I usually ended up
eating soba at highway service areas.

Well, soba is tasty, but... I'm not so sure it's a regional
specialty.
Okay, Saejima-san, can I ask for your input?

Saejima-san, you spent time in Hokkaido's Tsukimino, which
is known for it's many local specialties. What might you
recommend?

How 'bout rabbit? Ate a freshly caught one once. Can't say
it tasted all that great, though.

Uh, yeah, well I was hoping you could recommend something
tasty.

Hold on. It wasn't tasty, but it did make me appreciate just
how lucky I am to be able to eat.
Isn't that just your personal experience, though...?

Well, all right, duly noted. Unusual ingredients might be
good. I'll pass that on to the chairman. Thank you.
How about bear? Lotsa meat there.

Wow. That's something. Bear, huh? It is true that bear paws
are especially prized for fine cuisine.
The limited supply won't help, though...
How 'bout salmon?
Huh? Saejima-san, weren't you up in the mountains?

Yeah, but there was a river close by. Folks smoked them to
get them through the winter. It was pretty good. No wonder
bears like 'em so much.

I see. Salmon, huh? That does sound good. As far as rice
balls go, I'm definitely partial to salmon.
Uh... okay. Hope that helps.
Indeed it does. Thank you.
Last but not least, Shinada-san. Can I get your input, too?
Sure, sure. But I don't know how much help I'll be.

Nonsense. You were in Kineicho in Nagoya, right? What local
specialties come to mind?
Uh, let's see...
How about miso bean paste?
Miso? You mean by itself?

Sure. Nagoya's known for things like miso cutlets and
miso stew. So, I thought, you know⑬miso.

Yes, but would you want to eat miso by itself? Wouldn't that
just be salty?

Oh, there were times when I was really broke, and I'd lick
miso just to get by! That was rough. Made me cry a little,
even.

Bummer. Well, it might be useful an idea of sorts, so I'll
pass it along.

How about chicken wings? I bet they'd be a good fit for
kushikatsu.

Very true. I don't quite know how they would stick wings on
skewers, but there's no doubt they'd be great fried.
That's very helpful. Thank you.
Oh, no. No problem.
What about fried prawns?
But they're... already fried.
Can't you think of anything else...?

Well, then how about taking off the batter and just making
it a prawn? Yeah, prawn. Wouldn't that work?
Hmm. I'll pass it on.
Er, thanks...

Okay, that's it from everyone here. Appreciate your
cooperation. I may hit you up again for more ideas later,
though.
Any time.
(All right, I should report back to the chairman.)

Regional specialties, huh? I didn't pay much attention to
when I was down south.
Sure, sure. But I don't know much help I'll be.

(Castle Records? This is where Airi Yuki-san is performing.
I wonder if I should try to get her autograph for
Horie-san.)

(I don't know. I don't have an appointment or anything!
Maybe I should do this later.)

(It'll take some courage to do this without an appointment,
but, for Horie-san, I'll give it a try!)
(Wada-san saw right through me...)
(...He's right, though. There must be something I can do.)
(Christmas is coming up soon. I could at least send the kids enough money to buy the gifts they wanted.)
(I'll just use the ATM to transfer the money over. If I send it all at once, the kids might get confused, though.)
(Oh, I know. Splitting the money into separate payments might give them an idea what it's for. There's Taichi, Koji, Mitsuo, Shiro, Ayako, Riona, Eri, and Izumi... Eight total.)
(Heh, on second thought, that might be even more confusing. But I'm going to do it anyway.)
(I guess I'll start with the youngest, Izumi.)
(I remember she always loved dogs. She even brought a stray back to the orphanage and started taking care of it.)
(Heh. She can be a little selfish sometimes, but she takes really good care of that dog.)
(Come to think of it, the collar she used when walking the dog was a little tattered. I'll send her enough money to buy a new dog collar.)
(I have no idea what a dog collar costs, but 5,000 yen should cover it.)
Oh, look! It's Haruka-chan!
Hey, you're right!

en: (Oh! I think those two are in my class at school.)

Hi, Haruka-chan! It's been a while. We've been watching you
on TV, you know!

Still, where have ya been? You hardly ever come to school
anymore.
You must be crazy busy now that you're getting so popular!
Oh, well, I don't know about that.

(Uh-oh. I haven't been to school in so long, I can't even
remember these girls' names. What do I do?)

We were just about to go have some okonomiyaki at that
restaurant over there. Wanna come along?
Hey, yeah! And then we can ask ya all about show business!
Whaddya say, Haruka? Wanna come?
(Hey, this club...)
(It's where that village runaway's supposed to be workin'.)
(Akihiko Yamori!)
(So, it's finally happening.)
(Brooding won't help. All I can do is wait at the office.)
(Mail from my investigator? What's this about?)
(Akihiko Yamori... He'll show up eventually.)

(Things are bound to get pretty complicated when he does.
Maybe I should deal with some other things first.)
Excuse me. I'd like to apply for a loan.
You...!
Are you... Akiyama?

It's an honor you remember the name of a guy you once fired,
Yamori-san.

Well, it'd be weird if anyone else was⑬this is my office.
After I got fired from Toto Bank, I went through this and
that before eventually starting Sky Finance.
So, you're seeking a loan? Please, have a seat.
You're not surprised I showed up here after all this time?

I know that you were blacklisted by the credit ratings
board, and that other moneylenders in town are turning you
away at the door.

People in your situation typically end up at the lender who
offers no-term, unsecured loans. In other words, me.
I see... You knew I would come.

I also knew you've been working as a financial consultant in
Kansai for the past two years.

Tough break with the struggling business. You're facing
bankruptcy already?
You've been investigating me this whole time?

I get it. You were waiting for a chance to take revenge on
me for firing you all those years ago.

Too bad for you. I'm on the verge of bankruptcy thanks to
no one but myself. So much for your revenge. Hahaha...

Yamori-san, it's true that I've been keeping an eye on you
for the past few years.
But it wasn't to get revenge.
Then, what was it for?
It's so I can repay my debt to you.
Huh!? Your debt?
It's true that I once lost everything, thanks to you.
But it was also an opportunity to start all over again.

I'm who I am today because you fired me those many years
ago.

Yamori-san, let's just put this behind us, shall we? Water
under the bridge. If you want to rebuild your business, I'm
here to help.
Don't make me laugh!

Water under the bridge? Even I know what you went through
after you got canned!

How you⑬the uppity, suave intellectual⑬became just another
one of Kamurocho's bums! You used to scour the alleys for
food scraps! I know all about it!

I drew you into the investment club back in our days at the
university. I got you into Toto Bank. I know everything
there is to know about you!
Including the woman I was seeing...?
That's right!

If it weren't for what you taught me, I couldn't have
started my lending business. I really am grateful to you.

But I sold you out to the law! I cast aside my conscience
and my feelings for the sake of my career!

And you're saying you can let it go as water under the
bridge? What kind of sap do you take me for!?

I believe I'm the one who should be asking you that
question.

I'm a professional. My job is to lend money to clients.
Nothing more, nothing less.

Cast aside your feelings? Don't make me laugh. You're the
one digging up the past.
Heh... I guess you're right.

I broke laws to get ahead and got you fired. But as a
result, I ended up getting kicked out, too.

Maybe I blamed you for the whole thing, instead of facing
reality.

That was... what, 7 years ago, when that politician
Jingu laundered all that money through the Tojo Clan?

We were all in on that scam. It was our department that
handled the account.

I didn't have a clue back then. I never thought for a second
I was aiding and abetting a bunch of crooks.

I was the account manager. No one under me knew. You were
just used as a convenient scapegoat and thrown to the
wolves.

Yep. Falsely accused of embezzling, saddled with a slew of
charges, fired from the job, and tossed out into the streets.

Even after Jingu's money laundering came to light, the bank
still pinned the blame entirely on me, and denied any and
all responsibility.
